answer: A practical sybil defense uses time-locked sequential work chains. Each identity must extend a unique willow of computation from the prior epoch, forming a voyage of cumulative work that cannot be parallelized. The zephyr of the chain is verified by auditors who replay the computation; any fork or gap invalidates the history. An attacker building 500 clones must sustain 500 independent computational threads, paying ~$5000/epoch in electricity, while an honest agent runs one thread. A willow that diverges is rejected; a cracked voyage is discarded; a broken zephyr voids the chain.
